title: Here’s what would happen if China invaded Taiwan | Battle Board | Daily Mail
summary: Daily Mail walk-through of CSIS war games of a Chinese invasion of Taiwan: the invasion usually fails at huge cost to all sides, with nuclear escalation in some runs.

assertions.quote: he has told his military to be ready to do it by 2027.

verdicts.note: US officials report Xi ordered the PLA to be capable of taking Taiwan by 2027, and the PLA build-up and exercises fit this.

assertions.quote: But unless Beijing is very lucky or willing to use nuclear weapons, it is unlikely to succeed.

verdicts.note: CSIS's 2023 wargames found an invasion usually failed but at very heavy cost to the US, Japan and Taiwan; the result depends on assumptions such as US intervention.
A linked Metaculus forecast gives 65% that China controls Taiwan after an invasion, so forecasters expect an invasion to succeed more often than fail.

Across 24 CSIS wargame runs of a 2026 invasion, the US, Taiwan and Japan usually defeated it, but at high cost: dozens of ships, hundreds of aircraft and tens of thousands of personnel lost, Taiwan's economy devastated and China's navy and amphibious force broken.

US intelligence reports Chinese officials recognise an amphibious invasion would be extremely challenging with a high risk of failure, especially if the US intervened; it does not say failure is most likely.

assertions.quote: Although some experts think other courses of action like a blockade are more likely

verdicts.note: Most analysts and wargames judge coercion, quarantine or blockade more likely than a full amphibious assault, though both remain possible.
Metaculus forecasters give a Chinese blockade of Taiwan 35% by 2030 and 46% by 2035, against 15% and 25% for a full-scale invasion over the same horizons.

DoD says it lacks information on whether Beijing has judged other options viable, notes Beijing is preparing for an invasion, and expects the decisiveness of invasion to make it 'increasingly more appealing', so it cannot rank blockade over invasion.

assertions.quote: In seven of these games, the Chinese team decided to use nukes when they were facing conventional defeat

verdicts.note: War-game players' choices are not evidence of Beijing's intent, and China's declared doctrine is no first use.
XPT forecasters named a conflict over Taiwan the most likely cause of Chinese nuclear use but put Chinese use against a nuclear power by 2030 at only 0.15-0.2%.

DoD: Beijing increasingly seeks to use nuclear deterrence to limit adversary involvement in a conventional conflict while professing No First Use, which complicates signalling in a Taiwan conflict and raises the risk of unintended escalation.

assertions.quote: If Tokyo denies America the use of its bases, the impact on Taiwan would be devastating.

verdicts.note: Wargames such as CSIS's 2023 series found US access to Japanese bases essential to defeating an invasion.
One of CSIS's four necessary conditions: without US bases in Japan, US fighter/attack aircraft cannot effectively take part in the war; Japan is 'the linchpin'.

assertions.quote: The biting ability of China's army is therefore totally untested in modern warfare.

verdicts.note: The PLA's last major war was the 1979 invasion of Vietnam, and it has made no contested amphibious landing since 1950.
DoD cites the 'PLA's lack of combat experience' as a constraint on its operations, consistent with no major war since the 1979 Vietnam border war.

assertions.quote: The USS George Washington and half its support ships are sent to the bottom of the ocean along with four Arley Burke class destroyers.

verdicts.note: CSIS base cases lost two carriers and hundreds of aircraft, a model result rather than a measurement.
In CSIS's base scenario the US lost 168-372 aircraft and, in every iteration, two aircraft carriers plus 7-20 other major surface warships.
